summary.headline: Vaibhav Global Q1 FY27 EBITDA rose 37% YoY to Rs 102 crore, but reported gains were helped by Rs 25.5 crore US tariff refund and FX; constant-currency revenue was broadly flat.
summary.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 revenue of Rs 917 crore, EBITDA of Rs 102 crore (up 37% YoY, margin about 11% versus 9.2% a year earlier) and PAT of Rs 56 crore (up 50% YoY). Management said reported growth benefited from favourable foreign exchange and a US tariff refund, and that constant-currency revenue was broadly flat amid Middle East disruption and cautious US consumer spending. Analysts pressed on the tariff refund's accounting (recorded as other operating revenue, with questions on whether it sits in gross margin), the gap between digital revenue growth and volumes, and the Rs 5,000–5,500 crore FY30 vision. Management gave no hard margin guidance beyond saying gross margin and investment would keep improving.

financial_highlights.change: Broadly flat on constant-currency basis (as stated)
Included in Q1 FY27 reported numbers
As of 30 June 2026 (period reference as stated)
Management cited strength of vertically integrated model; analyst later flagged gross margin spike linked to the Rs 25.5 crore refund

segments.name: US
segments.commentary: Management said US consumer caution and subdued TSE (television shopping) business weighed; proprietary brand Rachel Galli performed strongly; vertically integrated model and diversified sourcing helped margins despite tariffs.

segments.name: UK
segments.commentary: UK performance described as flat; management cited momentum in two brands as basis for medium-term recovery confidence.

segments.name: Germany
segments.commentary: Achieved about break-even for full year FY26; management said it is now on track to contribute positively from FY27.

segments.name: B2C / Lifestyle
segments.commentary: Lifestyle products about 40% of B2C revenue this quarter against a medium-term target of 50%.

guidance_outlook: FY30 vision of Rs 5,000–5,500 crore revenue; analysts questioned feasibility at about 10% growth; management said levers are digital paid media, OTT, live TV and TikTok, and that European markets are under evaluation.
Management said gross margin will keep improving and investment will rise; no specific margin number was given.
Management said a Rs 100 million (USD) acquisition or internal strategy is being considered, without specifying a timeline.
Digital-first brand in India: management said a new leader may be placed in the US to explore it, with no committed timeline.
Digital customer profitability target: move from about 9–10 months to within 3 months, per management.
capex_capacity: No specific capex, capacity or utilisation figures were disclosed in the call.
Management referenced investment in digital and AI tools, headcount rationalisation, logistics efficiency and automation as cost levers.
demand_pricing: Revenue growth driven mainly by currency and tariff refund; ex-currency US dollar growth was described as volume-led but broadly flat.
US consumers were described as prioritising essentials over discretionary spending; management pointed to macro data showing discretionary categories still growing.

Analyst data: digital revenue up about 20%, ASP up about 10%, volumes roughly flat (about 0.7%), repeat rate about 23%, and about 3.5 lakh new digital users added in trailing 12 months; management did not reconcile these figures on the call.
Gross margin on native digital business said to be higher than TV business; digital ad spend hurdle rate referenced but not quantified clearly.

qa_highlights.question: Can the FY30 Rs 5,000–5,500 crore vision be reached with about 10% growth, and what margins are implied?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said gross margin will keep improving and investment will rise; it declined to give a specific margin number but said margins will improve.

qa_highlights.question: Why no buyback, and why not be more aggressive on India or digital given strong cash generation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it generates free cash flow and has an internal assessment for a USD 100 million strategy, not only acquisitions; an India digital brand idea is being considered with a possible new leader in the US.

qa_highlights.question: How much of revenue growth is currency, pricing and volume?
qa_highlights.answer: Largely currency and the tariff refund; ex-currency US dollar growth was described as flat to lower volume.

qa_highlights.question: How much was the tariff refund, where is it booked, and why not disclosed more clearly?
qa_highlights.answer: Refund of about Rs 25.5 crore booked in other operating revenue; management did not fully explain the gross margin effect on the call.

qa_highlights.question: Why is digital growth not matching volumes and repeats, and how is lab-grown diamond ASP trending?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not reconcile the volume, ASP and repeat figures; it said lab-grown diamonds are about 13% of revenue and it expects further growth from digital properties.

qa_highlights.question: How will digital affect the four customer-funnel stages (acquisition, retention, repeat), and how much growth is organic versus acquired?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said new-customer acquisition will accelerate, while retention and repeat may decline because digital customer lifetime value is lower than TV; the aim is to cut digital customer payback from 9–10 months to about 3 months.

risks_watch: Reported profit growth depends on a one-time Rs 25.5 crore US tariff refund and FX; ex-refund EBITDA growth is materially lower.
Constant-currency revenue flat; US consumer demand and TSE weakness persist.
Retention and repeat rates may fall as digital mix rises, given lower digital customer lifetime value.
Disclosure quality: analysts asked for country-level constant-currency growth and quantification of the refund, which were not provided on the call.
FY30 vision of Rs 5,000–5,500 crore needs about 10%+ CAGR; no capital allocation or buyback decision was announced.
summary.management_tone: Confident on digital investments and margin trajectory, but evasive on quantifying the tariff refund, constant-currency growth by country, and FY30 margin numbers. Management attributed weak organic growth to macro factors and avoided specific commitments.
key_quotes: Reported growth benefited from favorable foreign exchange and US tariff refund during the quarter.
Pleased to confirm that the business is now on track to contribute positively from FY27, consistent development.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade

rows.label: New product launch

rows.why: Management said European markets are under evaluation as a lever toward the Rs 5,000-5,500 crore FY30 vision, but gave no timing or size; Germany only reached about break-even in FY26.
